$comment: The pull-request label policy for this repository — the POLICY half; the checker that enforces it is ../.github/workflows/pr-labels.yml, and the two are separate for the same reason gates.json and cli/compile.mjs are. The set is derived from this repository's own structure rather than from GitHub's stock issue labels, which are built for bug trackers and cannot discriminate between changes here: every pull request in a doctrine repository would be `documentation`. Adding a label to this file does NOT create it on GitHub, and until it exists nobody can apply it — see the `gh label create` loop under 'Adding a label ... does not create it on GitHub' in memory/every-pull-request-carries-a-label.md.
policyMeans: A pull request carries at least one label from `labels` below. Extra labels beyond the set are allowed and ignored — the check refuses an UNLABELLED pull request, never an over-labelled one, because a rule that fails on a stray `question` is a rule someone switches off. WHICH label is right stays human judgement, exactly as the rationale half of a rule's provenance does (dod.md, condition 3); `covers` is the guidance, not a matcher.
$intake: The ISSUE-intake vocabulary, kept in a separate array from `labels` on purpose. `labels` is the PULL-REQUEST policy and `../.github/workflows/pr-labels.yml` reads `.labels[].name` and nothing else, so these three are invisible to that check — which is the point. Folding them into one set would let a pull request satisfy the at-least-one policy by being labelled `feedback`, and would ask an incoming bug report to know whether it is `doctrine` or `mechanism`, which a reporter cannot know and should not be asked. The two vocabularies answer different questions: `labels` says which part of the repository a change touched, `intake` says what kind of report arrived. Applied automatically by the issue forms in `../.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/`. As with `labels`, declaring one here does NOT create it on GitHub — see the `gh label create` note in memory/every-pull-request-carries-a-label.md.

intake.name: bug
intake.description: Something does not do what the files say it does
intake.note: Already existed on the repository — GitHub's stock label, and the one case where the stock vocabulary says exactly the right thing.

intake.name: improvement
intake.description: A proposed change to doctrine, mechanism, or the shape of a file
intake.note: Named `improvement` rather than reusing GitHub's stock `enhancement`, which reads as a feature request for a product with features. What arrives here is usually an argument about a standard.

intake.name: feedback
intake.description: Confusion, friction, or an expectation the files did not meet — neither a defect nor a proposal
intake.note: The category that has no stock equivalent, and the one this repository most needs: a file that does not land is a defect in a product whose product is its files, even when nothing is broken.

$ownership: The OWNERSHIP vocabulary — a third array for a third question. `labels` says which part of the repository a change touched; `intake` says what kind of report arrived; this says WHO DRIVES the pull request. Kept out of `labels` for the same reason `intake` is: ../.github/workflows/pr-labels.yml reads `.labels[].name` and nothing else, so a pull request can never satisfy the at-least-one policy by carrying `agent-driven` alone — ownership rides BESIDE an area label, never instead of one. The ruling behind it (the maintainer, 2026-07-29, verbatim: 'go with option B, wire the agent-driven label', on #95's refutation of assignee-as-ownership — a GitHub App's bot identity cannot be an assignee): authorship is the ownership carrier, and this label makes it filterable. Applied by ../.github/workflows/librarian.yml where nobody is present, and at `gh pr create` by the session that opens an agent-driven pull request — the convention is in ../gate-map.md's Propose tier. Forward-only: merged pull requests are not backfilled. As everywhere in this file, declaring does not create — `agent-driven` was created with `gh label create` on 2026-07-29.

ownership.name: agent-driven
ownership.description: An agent drives this pull request. Ownership rides authorship; this label makes it filterable.
ownership.appliedBy: librarian.yml for App-filed pull requests; the opening session otherwise

labels.name: doctrine
labels.description: The engine's own doctrine: core/, templates, skills, personas

labels.name: mechanism
labels.description: The code that checks and enforces: cli/, spec/, plugin/, .claude-plugin/

labels.name: record
labels.description: The audit trail: the plan's Session log, handoffs, the changelog

labels.name: infrastructure
labels.description: CI, workflows, repository and branch-protection settings

labels.name: dependencies
labels.description: Pull requests that update a dependency file
labels.note: Declared so a Dependabot pull request satisfies the policy with the label Dependabot applies itself. It cannot know this repository's vocabulary, and a gate that reds every automated security bump is a gate that gets bypassed. Same for github_actions below. Both already existed on the repository — created by Dependabot, not by this policy.

labels.name: github_actions
labels.description: Pull requests that update GitHub Actions code
